newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Sampoerna eyes 15 percent stake in Indofood.
newsitem.headline: Sampoerna eyes 15 percent stake in Indofood.

text.p: Indonesian tobacco tycoon Putera Sampoerna has long-term plans to take a 15 percent stake in noodle-maker PT Indofood Sukses Makmur, an aide said on Thursday.

Ekadharmajanto Kasih, chief financial officer of PT Handjaya Mandala Sampoerna, confirmed Sampoerna, founder and president director of the firm, had bought a 5.63 percent stake, or about 85.9 million Indofood shares, at 5,800 rupiah each.
He said Sampoerna's purchase was made in his personal capacity on Tuesday on the Surabaya Stock Exchange through a cross-trade.
Indofood closed at 5,775 rupiah on the Jakarta bourse on Thursday, unchanged on a volume of 3.9 million shares after rising to a high of 6,100 rupiah earlier.
"For long-term planning, Sampoerna plans to have about a 15 percent stake in Indofood," Kasih said.
He said Putera Sampoerna's acqusition of a stake in Indofood could open the possibility of cooperation between PT Sampoerna and Indofood, which is part of the Salim Group.
Asked if Sampoerna had set any time-frame for greater involvement in Indofood, Kasih said it was believed that Indofood had good business prospects beyond 2000.
"Principally, if the stocks are available in the market with a good price, we will be buying it," Kasih added.
He said Sampoerna talked with Indofood before the deal.
"Indofood's founders welcomed Sampoerna having a substantial stake in their company," he said, adding that "substantial" could be interpreted as between five to 15 percent.
Kasih said PT Sampoerna and PT Indofood could work together in areas such as distribution.
"We have Alfa Retail and Indofood has Indomarco. Both are involved in distribution. Maybe we can merge (in this sector)," he said.
The move took place the day after Indofood said the price of a planned series of acquisitions of sister companies had dropped to 1.55 trillion rupiah from the previous 1.75 trillion rupiah.
The company said the price was reduced "to give more value to public shareholders".
The acquisition plan, under which Indofood was to acquire six units of the Salim Group, of which it is also a member, has drawn some adverse reactions.
Analysts have said the plan does not offer shareholders tangible benefits and had said the 1.75 trillion rupiah price was too high.
"After Indofood lowered the acquisition price, I believe they will win shareholders' approval," an analyst with a Japanese securities house said.
She added that in the long term, the planned acquisitions were good for investors and would give a high return. "The new price is attractive," she said, without elaborating.
Analysts and brokers said the entry of Sampoerna into Indofood would boost shareholder sentiment ahead of its extraordinary general meeting on its acquisition plans on April 3.
